newsitem.title: CANADA: Vanclief faces heavy load as Canada farm minister.
newsitem.headline: Vanclief faces heavy load as Canada farm minister.

text.p: The chairman of the House of Commons Agriculture Committee, Ontario-based Lyle Vanclief, on Wednesday took over the Agriculture Ministry portfolio from Ralph Goodale, who becomes Natural Resources Minister.
The new agriculture minister will have to grapple with grain transportation issues, especially rail transport rates which are currently capped.

But the heavy responsibility of modernizing the Canadian Wheat Board, one of the world's oldest and largest state commodity export monopolies, will stay with Goodale as he moves over to Natural Resources.

Under the last parliament, Goodale said if he were reappointed to the position, he would reintroduce amendments to the CWB Act, which propose to modernize the CWB's governance to a farmer-elected board of directors from the current government-appointed commissioners.

Under Goodale's plan, membership in the CWB would still be mandatory. The new government will likely face competing pressures from the farming sector, with one side backing a continued mandatory monopoly and the other side pushing for a voluntary organization.
Canada is the second largest seller of wheat to the world. The CWB, Canada's fifth largest exporter, made C$5.8 billion in wheat and barley sales in the 1995/96 crop year (Aug/July).
